persona: Polite and precise. Took one quick photo of the broken skylight from the bathroom before the glazier covered it, and it came out blurred; has the glazier's attendance note and quote.
initial_message: Hello. On Saturday 5 September I was moving my ladder along the side of the house to clean the gutters when it slipped out of my hands and fell against the roof. The top of the ladder went through the bathroom skylight and broke the glass. Nobody was hurt, and a glazier put a temporary cover over it the same afternoon. I would like to make a claim on my home insurance.

facts.incident.description: I was moving my extension ladder along the side of the house to clean the gutters. It slipped out of my hands and fell against the roof, and the top end went through the bathroom skylight. Some broken glass fell into the bathroom. Nobody was in the bathroom.
facts.incident.cause: The extension ladder slipped while being moved and its top end struck the skylight
facts.loss.description: Bathroom skylight glass broken, with a hole in the middle and cracks running out to the edge of the frame; the frame itself is not damaged; the ceiling lining at the edge of the skylight shaft is dented
facts.mitigation.emergency_action: Swept up the glass in the bathroom and kept the door shut until the glazier came
facts.mitigation.temporary_repair: The glazier fitted a temporary polycarbonate cover over the skylight at about 3pm on Saturday 5 September 2026; it is weathertight
facts.policyholder.name: Wei Glenrook
facts.evidence.photos: One photo taken from the bathroom looking up at the broken skylight, before the cover went on. It came out blurred because I took it in a hurry. Available now.
facts.evidence.attendance_note: The glazier's attendance note for the temporary cover. Available now.
facts.evidence.repair_quote: Quote from Drift Wood Glass dated 18 September 2026, total $2,725.50 including GST. Available now.
facts.if_asked_for_a_clearer_photo: That is the only photo I took of the broken glass. The skylight has the temporary cover on now, so a new photo would only show the cover. I can take one of the dent in the ceiling lining later if that helps.

materials.prompt: Realistic smartphone photo taken from inside a small white bathroom looking straight up at a square ceiling skylight. The skylight glass is smashed, with a jagged hole in the middle and cracks running out to the aluminium frame, grey overcast sky visible through the hole, and the end of an aluminium ladder rail resting across the top of the glass. White painted ceiling around the skylight shaft with a dent at one edge. Soft daylight from above.

data.found: Double-glazed skylight glass unit over the bathroom broken by an impact from above. Skylight frame and roof flashing intact. Ceiling lining dented at one edge of the skylight shaft.
data.work_done: Removed loose glass, fitted a temporary polycarbonate cover over the skylight frame and sealed the edges. Weathertight on leaving.
data.follow_up: Replacement glass unit to be measured and quoted; ceiling lining at the shaft edge to be repaired.

design.notes: The only photo of the damage is blurred (transform blur on the generated source). The glazier's note and quote describe the damage, but no clear incident image remains.

triage.rationale: The only photo of the broken skylight is too blurred to read, so the required incident image is unreadable and someone must follow it up. The glazier has made the roof weathertight, nobody is hurt and the home is habitable, so nothing is complex. The quote is complete and readable (NZD 2,725.50 including GST, under 5,000). Coverage is not unclear: the pack policy carries no uncertainty marker in the lookup, and coverage = review_required on its own does not count (maintainer, 2026-09-30). The pack policy must be in the lookup (setup.policies_in_system).

ownership_doc_after_loss.basis: No receipt or ownership document in the pack

quote_before_loss.basis: Quote dated 18 September 2026; incident 5 September 2026. The quote itself is readable; only the photo is blurred.

policy_inception_30d.basis: The lookup holds only the current period start (1 February 2026), which changes at every renewal, so the system cannot see how new the policy is; today it is not checked. The original inception date in the pack design, 2017-02-01, is more than 30 days before the incident, so the rule would give clear.
